handbookNote: Washington Revised Code Chapter 42.45, the Uniform Law on Notarial Acts (a genuine RULONA adoption), 28 substantive sections (RCW 42.45.010-42.45.280) plus miscellaneous 900-series provisions, retrieved directly from app.leg.wa.gov -- compiled source at temp/handbooks/wa/notary.txt. CLASSIFICATION: application-only. RCW 42.45.200 (qualifications) contains no exam or training-course requirement anywhere in its text -- an applicant need only be 18+, a Washington resident or have a WA place of employment/practice, able to read and write English, execute an oath of office, and post a surety bond; the NNA also states plainly that 'no training or exam is required' for Washington notaries. This track is a self-study/reference practice-question set grounded in real state notary law, not exam prep. ADMINISTRATION QUIRK: Washington notaries are administered by the DEPARTMENT OF LICENSING (the 'director' throughout the statute means the director of licensing or designee) -- NOT the secretary of state, which is the more common arrangement in most other states. CONTENT DEPTH: a full, richly detailed RULONA chapter -- 18 defined terms, five parallel sections on recognizing notarial acts performed in-state/other-state/tribal/federal/foreign jurisdictions (with a consistent prima-facie-vs-conclusive evidentiary distinction running through all five), a 7-subsection certificate-of-notarial-act section, 6 short certificate forms, a 10-subsection commission/qualifications/bond section, a 10-ground discipline section, a 6-subsection prohibited-acts section (including a notario-publico use restriction and a mandatory non-attorney disclosure statement), and a fully built-out remote/electronic notarization framework at RCW 42.45.190 and .280 (tamper-evident technology selection, dual identity-proofing for remote signers, 10-year audiovisual-recording retention, and special conditions for remotely located signers outside the U.S.) -- comparable in depth to the richest application-only notary states already scoped in this project, supporting the ~150-200 question ceiling rather than the ~100 typical of thinner states. NOTABLE QUIRKS embedded in the question set: (1) Department of Licensing administration rather than Secretary of State; (2) a surety bond is required under RCW 42.45.200(4), but the dollar amount is delegated entirely to director rule (WAC), not fixed in the RCW text itself, so questions test the bond's structural requirements (licensed surety, 4-year term or commission-coterminous, 30-day cancellation notice, 30-day claim-payment notice) rather than asserting a specific dollar figure not actually present in the statute; (3) commission term is 4 years, capped earlier by the assurance's expiration date if shorter (RCW 42.45.200(5)); (4) RCW 42.45.280 (remote/electronic notarization) as fetched has TWO versions on the same official page -- the version 'effective until January 1, 2027' (used as the primary basis for this question set, since it governs through virtually this track's entire practical shelf life) and a version 'effective January 1, 2027' (per 2026 c 21 / HB 2158) that adds tangible-record remote-notarization procedures, remote oath administration, and an agent-for-service-of-process provision -- one question explicitly flags this forthcoming change for durability. PRICING: $0.99 (99 cents) -- this project's bottom self-serve tier for application-only notary states, reflecting that no exam/course prep value is being sold, only a grounded statutory practice-question reference.
